title: Death Toll Rises to 160 in Nepal Flood as 133 Indian Pilgrims Remain Missing
excerpt: At least 57 Tamil Nadu pilgrims stranded in Rasuwa as rescue operations struggle with destroyed bridges, roads, and adverse weather across the Himalayan border region.
body:
• Death toll in Nepal-Tibet border flood rises to 160, with 403 travelers still missing including 133 Indian pilgrims en route to Mount Kailash
  • At least 57 Tamil Nadu pilgrims remain stranded in Rasuwa district, with 22 from Kumbakonam rescued and moved to a Nepal Army camp
  • Foreign nationals missing include 47 Americans, 34 Australians, 33 British, and 24 Canadians; rescue operations hampered by destroyed infrastructure
  • Floods destroyed 19 bridges, damaged 40 km of roads, and swept away roughly 200 vehicles, severely limiting ground-based rescue efforts

The death toll from Wednesday's catastrophic flash flood along the Nepal-Tibet border has climbed to 160, with at least 133 Indian pilgrims among the 403 travelers still unaccounted for, according to Nepal police and the country's tourism board.

The updated figures mark a sharp increase from initial reports and underscore the scale of the disaster, which struck at approximately 8:30 a.m. local time when a massive wall of mud and rock collapsed into the Bhote Koshi River in Nepal's northern Rasuwa district.

Indian Pilgrims Bear the Brunt

Sunil Sharma, a Nepal Tourism Board spokesperson, told the Associated Press that 133 of the missing tourists were Indian nationals on pilgrimage to Mount Kailash in Tibet, a site sacred to Hindus. Of the 403 missing, 341 are foreign nationals — 47 from the United States, 34 from Australia, 33 from Britain, and 24 from Canada.

At least 57 pilgrims from Tamil Nadu remain stranded in the Timure area of Rasuwa district. The group, hailing from Chennai, Kumbakonam, and other parts of the state, had been traveling through Nepal on a religious pilgrimage when the floods cut off road access. A separate group of 22 pilgrims from Kumbakonam has been rescued and moved to a Nepal Army camp, where they are receiving temporary accommodation.

"We have asked both India and China to help us with the rescue efforts."

— Sasmit Pokharel, Nepal Government Spokesperson

Rescue Operations Face Massive Obstacles

The floods have destroyed approximately 19 bridges, damaged nearly 40 kilometers of roads, and swept away around 200 vehicles — compounding what was already one of the most challenging rescue operations in Nepal's recent history. Helicopters deployed to evacuate stranded travelers have been unable to land in several locations due to high water levels and adverse weather conditions.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke with his Nepali counterpart and conveyed condolences. "India is ready to provide all possible humanitarian assistance to Nepal," Modi said on X. "Our teams are coordinating closely on rescue and relief efforts."

What Triggered the Disaster

Scientists analyzing satellite imagery from Planet Labs confirmed that a substantial portion of a glacier snout collapsed, likely triggered by a magnitude 4.4 earthquake reported by the U.S. Geological Survey about 100 kilometers north of Kathmandu. The collapse sent a torrent of ice, rock, and sediment into the valley, generating a debris-laden flood that devastated communities along the river.

"In order for this magnitude of floodwater and debris to come downstream there has to be a gigantic landmass or ice break."

— Umesh Haritashya, Professor of Geosciences, University of Dayton

Earth scientist Dan Shugar of the University of Calgary noted significant snowmelt in the 24 hours before the disaster, suggesting warm conditions may have contributed to the glacier's instability.

A Critical Window for Survivors

Though the current monsoon season is less favorable for trekking in Nepal, it is a major season for Kailash pilgrimages in Tibet, which follow a route through Rasuwa district near Tibet's Gyirong crossing. On the Chinese side, a mudslide struck the Gyirong Port border crossing, cutting roads, communications, and power links. Chinese President Xi Jinping called for an all-out rescue effort.

Eight South Korean workers at a hydropower plant in the area were separately reported missing. At least 28 Nepali police officials were also unaccounted for, according to police spokesperson Abi Narayan Kafle.

With night falling on the disaster zone and weather conditions deteriorating, rescue officials warned that the window for finding survivors was narrowing. Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority confirmed the flood was one of the deadliest natural disasters in the country's recent history.
nri_angle: Over 133 Indian nationals, many on pilgrimage to Mount Kailash, are among hundreds missing after the catastrophic flood; 57 Tamil Nadu pilgrims remain stranded.
